sessions.title: Identification
sessions.description:
How do we come to see ourselves as subjects?

What is the Lacanian mirror stage in developmental terms?

What is the ego in relation to the subject?

materials.title: The mirror-stage as formative of the I function as revealed in psychoanalytic experience
materials.note: Lacan, J. (2006). In B. Fink (Trans.), Écrits (pp 75-81). New York & London: W.W Norton.

sessions.title: Authority
sessions.description:
How does authority call upon us?

How does Ideology pervade our daily lives and our conceptions of ourselves?

What was Althusser’s contribution to ideology critique?

What is identification in Lacanian terms and how does this relate to the function of ideology?

Why do we obey?

materials.title: Ideology and ideological state apparatuses
materials.note: Althusser, L. (1971). In L. Althusser (Ed.), Lenin and philosophy and other essays. New York: Monthly Review Press.

sessions.title: the Sublime Object
sessions.description:
In what way does Zizek depart from the Althusserian notion of ideology?

How is ideology tied to desire and fantasy?

What is the relationship between desire and the Other?

How is the subject an answer to the Real?

sessions.title: Desire
sessions.description:
In what way is desire constructed?

What does capitalism get right about our desire?

In what ways is desire a political phenomenon?

Does desire escape power? Or does it become part of power’s relay network?

materials.title: Capitalism and Desire: The Psychic Cost of Free Markets

sessions.title: Race and Colonialism
sessions.description:
What is the psychology of colonization?

How does the colonial experience shape the psyche of the colonizer and the colonized?

What is the role of identification in colonial domination?

materials.title: A Critical Psychology of the Postcolonial

sessions.title: Patriarchy and Feminism
sessions.description:
How does patriarchy become normalized?

What is the political function of feminist critique?

How does patriarchy and other modes of authority lend support to each other?

sessions.title: Naming
sessions.description:
How is naming political?

What role does naming play in placing us within social and political structures?

What if we had no names?

materials.title: Through the Looking Glass and What Alice Found There
Ideology and ideological state apparatuses (cont’d)
materials.note: Althusser, L. (1971). In L. Althusser (Ed.), Lenin and philosophy and other essays. New York: Monthly Review Press.

sessions.title: Medical Power, Biopower, and the Power over Life and Death
sessions.description:
What is the productive side of power?

How does power produce pleasures, goods, and life?

How does power ostracize the deviant and the abnormal?

How did Foucault and the anti-psychiatry movement oppose psychology and psychoanalysis? Is there a way to reconcile Foucault’s theories with a psychoanalytical framework?

sessions.title: The Seduction of Technology
sessions.description:
To what extent have technology and cybernetics become part of our consciousness? What revisions can this technological turn offer to extant theories of subjectivity, identification, and desire?

How does technology make us complicit with power?

What modes of domination and violence are being sanitized and/or hidden behind shiny screens and slick keyboards?

Why do we trust the algorithm?
